Surah al-Qiyamah (The Resurrection) [Meccan, and its verses are forty verses]

﴿Lā﴾ is extra (zā'idah) in both places.

Nay, I swear by the self-reproaching soul (﴿ولا أُقْسِم بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوّامَة﴾), that blames itself even if it strives in doing good. The answer to the oath (jawab al-qasam) is omitted, i.e., لَتُبْعَثُنَّ (*la-tub'athunna*), "you will surely be resurrected," which is indicated by it:

Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: ﴿Does man think﴾, i.e., the disbeliever, ﴿that We will not assemble his bones﴾ for the resurrection and the revival.

Yes, [We are able to] gather them [together, (qadirin)] being able [to do so, together with gathering the rest of him], [to make even his fingertips (banan)], which are the fingers, [i.e., We are able to restore their bones as they were, despite their smallness; so how much more the large bones].

﴿Nay, man wishes to persist in wickedness﴾. The lām (اللام) is superfluous (زائدة, zā'idah), and it places the verb in the subjunctive (نصبه), governed by an implied أن (an, "that") which is understood (مقدرة, muqaddarah). The meaning is أن يُكَذِّب (an yukadhdhiba), "that he should deny." ﴿ahead of him﴾ (أمامه), i.e., the Day of Resurrection, which is indicated by:
﴿He asks when﴾ (it will be) ﴿the Day of Resurrection﴾, a question asked in mockery and denial.
﴿So when the sight is dazzled﴾: the ra' in بَرِقَ may be read with a kasra or with a fatha. Its meaning is that it is stunned and bewildered by what it sees, which it had been denying.
﴿And the moon is eclipsed﴾ it grew dark and its light departed.
"And the sun and the moon are joined together" — so they rise from the west, or their light is gone; and that is on the Day of Resurrection.
﴿On that Day, man will say, "Where is the escape?"﴾ *al-Firar*: the flight, the escape.
No, [there is] no refuge (kallā). A rebuke against seeking escape. ﴿There is no refuge﴾: no place of shelter to take cover in.
To your Lord, on that Day, is the resting-place (al-mustaqarr), the place where creatures come to rest, so they will be reckoned with and recompensed.
﴿He will be informed on that Day of what he sent forward and what he left behind﴾ with his first deed and his last.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 14:

﴿Nay, but man is a witness against himself﴾ (a witness) whose limbs speak of his deeds. The ha' (in baṣīrah) is for emphasis (lil-mubālaghah), so there is no escaping its recompense.

﴿Even if he should present his excuses﴾. "Ma'adhir" is the plural of "ma'dhira" (excuse), formed irregularly (ʿalā ghayr qiyās, i.e., not according to the regular rule of plural formation). The meaning is: even if he were to come with every excuse, it would not be accepted from him.

Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿before Gabriel has finished with it﴾, ﴿so that you may hasten with it﴾, out of fear that it will slip away from you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection﴾ in your breast, ﴿and its recitation﴾ your reciting it, i.e., its flowing upon your tongue.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 18:**

﴿So when We recite it﴾: upon you, with the recitation of Jibril. ﴿then follow its recitation﴾: listen to its recitation. So he (ﷺ) would listen to it, and then he would recite it.

Then indeed upon Us is its clarification (﴿ثُمَّ إنّ عَلَيْنا بَيانه﴾), by making you understand it. The connection between this verse and what precedes it is that the earlier verse included turning away from the signs of God, while this verse includes hastening toward them by memorizing them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 20:

﴿Kalla﴾ is an opening particle (istiftah) with the meaning of "Alā" (truly, indeed), ﴿bal tuhibbūna al-‘ājila﴾ ("Nay, but you love the hasty [life]"), meaning the world (al-dunyā), with the verbs read with both the yāʾ and the tāʾ.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 21:

﴿And you leave the Hereafter﴾, so they do not work for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 22:

﴿Faces on that Day﴾, i.e., on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿radiant﴾, beautiful and luminous.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 23:

﴿To their Lord they will be looking﴾. That is, they will see Allah, glorified and exalted be He, in the Hereafter.
﴿And faces that Day will be grim﴾ (scowling, intensely frowning)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 25:

﴿They are certain﴾ (tuqin) ﴿that a calamity will be inflicted upon them﴾: a great catastrophe that breaks the spine.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 26:

﴿Kallā﴾ (meaning "Alā," i.e., "Truly" or "Indeed") ﴿idhā balaghati al-nafs al-tarāqiya﴾ — meaning, when the soul reaches the collarbones, the bones of the throat.
{Wa qīla} — it is said, by those around him: {man rāq} — "Who is a reciter (of charms)?" meaning: who will recite over him (yarqīhi) so that he may be healed (li-yushfā).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 28:

﴿And he thought﴾ — i.e., he became certain — whoever's soul has reached this point, ﴿that it was the parting﴾ — i.e., the parting from this world.

﴿And one leg will be wrapped around the other﴾, i.e., one of his legs around the other at death; or, the intensity of parting from this world is wrapped together with the intensity of turning toward the Hereafter.

﴿To your Lord, that Day, is the driving.﴾ That is, al-sawq (the driving). This indicates the governing element (al-'amil) of إذا (idha, "when"). The meaning is: when the soul reaches the throat, it is driven to the judgment of its Lord.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 31:

﴿So he did not believe [in the truth]﴾, the man, ﴿nor did he pray﴾; i.e., he did not believe and did not pray.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 32:

﴿But he denied﴾ the Qur'an ﴿and turned away﴾ from faith.
﴿Then he went to his family, swaggering.﴾ He strutted in his gait out of self-admiration.

﴿Woe to you﴾. In it there is an iltifat (a shift in grammatical person) away from the third person (ghaybah). The word is an ism fi'l (a noun functioning as a verb), and the lam is lam al-tabyin (the lam of clarification). That is, what you dislike is nearer to you. ﴿And woe again﴾, i.e., it is more fitting for you than for anyone else.
﴿Then woe to you, and woe!﴾ (Tawkid, emphasis)

﴿Does man think﴾ يَظُنّ (he supposes) ﴿that he will be left﴾ هَمْلًا (neglected, without purpose) ﴿to roam aimlessly?﴾ لا يُكَلَّف بِالشَّرائِعِ (not charged with the sharia, the religious laws). لا يَحْسَب ذَلِكَ (let him not suppose that).

Qur'an 75:37: "Was he not a drop of semen emitted (in the womb)?"

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn): ﴿Was he not﴾, i.e., he was (كان) ﴿a drop of semen emitted﴾, read with the yā' and with the tā' (يُمْنى), which is poured into the womb (الرَّحِم).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 75, verse 38:

﴿Then he was﴾ a drop of semen, ﴿a clot of blood, and He created﴾ Allah, from it, the human being ﴿and proportioned him﴾, i.e., He made his limbs balanced and proportionate.

﴿Then He made of it﴾ — from the semen which became a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh — ﴿two mates﴾, the two kinds, ﴿the male and the female﴾, who sometimes come together and sometimes each one separates from the other.
﴿Is not that One﴾ who does these things ﴿able to give life to the dead?﴾ He (ﷺ) said, "Yes."
